I am getting old now, 76, but I still know my land. My son helps sometimes but mostly it is me and my wife. 21.4 mu is not small — I cannot do it all by hand like before, so I hire the tractor for plowing and use the well pump for water.

Last year the wheat and maize gave me decent yield, so I will do the same again. No reason to change what worked. I put about 15 mu into wheat-maize rotation — that is the main income. I keep 4 mu for cotton because the price has been okay, and 2.4 mu near the house for chili since my wife manages those and we can sell fresh at the market.

For wheat I use the improved Jimai seed — everyone in the village uses it now. I put about 18 kg nitrogen per mu, split between base fertilizer and topdressing at green-up. Phosphorus about 8 kg, potassium 6 kg. I irrigate at green-up, jointing, and grain-filling, sometimes a fourth time if spring is dry. Two sprays for aphids and rust. Yield around 500 kg per mu if weather holds.

For maize after wheat, I use hybrid Zhengdan or Xianyu, whatever the dealer has. Nitrogen 17 kg per mu — maize is hungry. Phosphorus 6, potassium 6. Two irrigations — jointing and tasseling. Two sprays for borer and armyworm. I expect 600 kg per mu.

Cotton I have grown for years. Bt hybrid saves me spraying for bollworm, but I still need sprays for aphids and spider mites — 6 times or so. Nitrogen 14 kg, phosphorus 7, potassium 8. Four irrigations. Cotton gives maybe 280 kg lint per mu.

Chili is my wife's pride. It needs the most work and the most fertilizer — nitrogen 22, phosphorus 15, potassium 20. Lots of water, six or seven times. Seven sprays because pests love chili. But the price is good, so it pays.

I plow deep every two or three years and rotary-till otherwise — the soil here packs down with the tractor.
